name: West African drumming
summary: Drum-and-dance music of West Africa: ensembles of bells, rattles and drums in which a short bell phrase, the timeline, guides interlocking parts and a lead drum talks over them. The commonest timeline is the seven-stroke standard pattern in a twelve-pulse cycle, and three against two is the basic cross-rhythm. Ewe dance-drumming of Ghana and Togo is the best documented case in this model.

drum_characteristics.feel: Mostly ternary: four main beats of three pulses, felt with six and three against them
drum_characteristics.subdivision: 12/8 (a twelve-pulse bell cycle); some pieces are in duple time
hallmarks: a bell timeline that guides every other part
three against two (six against four) as the basic cross-rhythm
a lead drum in dialogue with a response drum and the dancers
avoid: a snare backbeat as the frame

evidence.note: No tempo range: the tradition is too broad for one. Agbekor's is on style:agbekor.
